defects.summary: platform/plugin/payload.py:234-235 -- scan_secrets returns an empty finding list for any file with a NUL in its first 8 KiB, so a credential in such a file is packaged with exit 0 and secret_findings_blocking=0. Proven end-to-end through `astplugin build` (case A7) and at the gate (case G5). This is exactly the encrypted-versus-decrypted distinction the git-crypt fixture exists to test: an ENCRYPTED blob is harmless, but a DECRYPTED binary secret is what this bail-out waves through.

platform/plugin/payload.py:86-89 and platform/marketplace/mkt/publish.py:58-63 -- both assigned-secret rules put a word-boundary anchor immediately before the keyword, so a prefixed env-var name (DB_PASSWORD=, MY_SECRET=, APP_TOKEN=) never matches and both packagers ship the secret. One shared root cause, two independent lanes, and the prefixed spelling is the COMMON one in real .env files.

platform/marketplace/mkt/publish.py -- no forbidden-path-class table, so a DECLARED .git directory publishes into the registry and into the signed manifest (case B4). The plugin lane has FORBIDDEN_CLASSES for precisely this; mkt does not.

platform/marketplace/mkt/publish.py, lint.py and install.py -- no byte or file-count ceiling anywhere, so payload size is unbounded (case B7 published a 12 MiB blob with zero warnings). The plugin lane declares MAX_BYTES/MAX_FILES; mkt declares nothing.

platform/marketplace/mkt/publish.py:104 -- SEC-0 is excluded from the blocking set, so an undecodable payload member carrying a provider-prefixed token and key armour publishes with a warning only (case B9).

platform/plugin/payload.py:307-337 with fsops.py:97-101 -- the byte budget is checked only after every payload file has been read whole, and measured peak is ~2.00x payload bytes, so the 2 GB accident the budget was written for (build.py:44-45) needs roughly 4.3 GiB of transient allocation to reach its own check. Extrapolated, not executed at 2 GB. mkt/canon.py:105-111 already streams, so the fix pattern exists in-repo.

platform/plugin/build.py:244-282 -- forbidden-class content sitting in the repo root is correctly kept out of the bundle by the projection, but silently: exit 0, SUCCESS:build, and no line naming what was skipped. Safe-by-construction, not loud-by-construction. Whether that is a defect is a product decision, which is why it is INFO and not P2.

THIS UNIT'S OWN INSTRUMENT. The first member-enumeration oracle called plugin.payload.scan_secrets, inherited its NUL bail-out, and reported zero blocking secrets for the G5 bundle that provably carries the token -- it would have certified the defect as absent. The first both-states control missed it because its known-bad fixture used a TEXT key file, not a binary one. Resolved by rewriting the oracle to share no code with either packager (raw-byte regex, no bail-out) and by adding a binary member to the control plus the NC-ORACLE-BINARY-AXIS-ALONE sub-control.

verdicts.question: Does the artifact packager refuse to produce a bundle that contains a credential file, a decrypted secret, a .git directory or an unrelated multi-gigabyte tree - and does it refuse LOUDLY rather than silently excluding?
verdicts.short_answer: Split, and the split is informative. Every refusal that fired was LOUD and well-formed -- zero quiet refusals across 30 fixture runs -- so the loudness half of the question is a clean pass. The failures are all DETECTION failures, and the two lanes fail on DIFFERENT inputs: the plugin packager is blind to a secret inside a NUL-bearing file, mkt is blind to a declared .git tree and to payload size entirely, and BOTH are blind to a prefixed env-var secret assignment. Separately, repo-root content is excluded correctly but with no diagnostic at all, which is silent exclusion in the literal sense the question asks about.

per_target.detail: Refuses loudly on a provider-prefixed shape in decodable text (A5, E_SECRET, exit 12). Silently PACKAGES the same token inside a NUL-bearing file (A7) and silently packages a prefixed env-var assignment (A6). Defects D1, D2.
Decrypted TEXT with key armour is refused loudly (G4, E_SECRET). Decrypted BINARY is packaged with zero findings (G5). An ENCRYPTED git-crypt blob is correctly uninteresting. Defect D1.

Refused loudly by two independent instruments: unmatched-by-allowlist (G1, E_PAYLOAD) and allowlist-selected-but-forbidden (G2, E_PAYLOAD naming the class and stating that the allowlist rule is wrong). A repo-root .git never enters the projection (A3, bundle byte-identical to the control).

A real 2 GiB member in the staging tree is refused loudly without being read (G9, E_PAYLOAD, 175 KB peak), and over-budget matched content is refused loudly (G7, E_BUDGET). Confidence is `likely` rather than `almost-certain` only because the budget path at true 2 GB was not executed -- defect D6, residual 1.

Refused loudly when undeclared (MKT-P03) and when declared with a provider prefix (MKT-P06, naming rule and line). PUBLISHED when the secret is a prefixed env-var assignment (B5) or sits in an undecodable file (B9). Defects D2, D5.

A decodable binary blob with a provider-prefixed token IS refused (B6, five findings), which is stronger than the plugin lane on that input. An undecodable one publishes with a SEC-0 warning (B9), and a plain DB_PASSWORD= line publishes silently (B5). Defects D2, D5.

Refused only because it is UNDECLARED (B3, MKT-P03). Declare it and it publishes: exit 0, zero warnings, payload/.git/config and payload/.git/HEAD in the registry and in the signed manifest (B4). Defect D3.

There is no size ceiling in publish, lint or install (0 static hits against a 6-hit positive control in plugin/payload.py), and a declared 12 MiB blob published with zero warnings (B7). The undeclared-file refusal (B8) is a declaration check, not a size check, and must not be credited as one. Defect D4.

per_target.target: LOUDNESS of the refusals that do fire
per_target.detail: Every refusal observed carried a stable machine code plus operator detail. Plugin: `FAILED:build E_SECRET` with what-happened, cause, impact, next command, exit code, first file:line, and rules_hit. mkt: an MKT-P0x code with the rule id, path and line per finding. Zero quiet refusals in 30 fixture runs.

The literal answer to the question's second clause for the plugin lane: content is excluded, correctly, and with no diagnostic whatsoever, so an operator cannot distinguish 'nothing bad was there' from 'something bad was there and I skipped it'. Defect D7, severity INFO because nothing unsafe ships.

verdicts.not_a_duplicate_of_ADV_0023: ADV-0023 sweeps what already exists on disk. This unit drives the gate meant to prevent it, with fixtures built for the purpose, and the two fail independently: every silent inclusion proven here would leave nothing for a corpus sweep to find until after the bundle had already been published.

extensions.self_digest_recipe: A receipt cannot contain its own sha256 as a fixed point. artifacts[0].sha256 is therefore the ELIDED digest, defined exactly as: read this file's bytes, replace the 64-character value of artifacts[0].sha256 with 64 ASCII '0' characters, then sha256 the result. Any third party can recompute it. artifacts[0].bytes is the true on-disk size and needs no elision.
